title: Private Token
summary: A new token with encrypted balances
description: Launches a brand-new Encrypted ERC in standalone mode: supply is created by private mints from the owner, balances and transfer amounts stay encrypted, and an auditor can decrypt. Total supply stays private too.
prompts: Launch a token where balances are private
Create a confidential points or rewards token
Issue a private security token with an auditor

main.description: Fuji C-Chain, which has the shared eERC registrar, verifiers and library

params.name: owner
params.description: Owns the token and performs private mints

params.name: auditor
params.description: Can decrypt every amount; must be registered with the registrar

params.name: mintAmount
params.description: Smoke-test mint to the builder, in 2-decimal units; the default is 100.00

prerequisites: A browser wallet that can sign messages: eERC keys and proofs are made on the builder's device

contracts.name: EncryptedERC
contracts.description: The eERC contract, deployed in standalone mode

contracts.name: Registrar
contracts.description: Shared registry of users' BabyJubJub public keys

steps.title: Register the auditor's eERC key
steps.notes: Skipped when Registrar.isUserRegistered(auditor) is already true.

steps.title: Register the builder's eERC key
steps.notes: A no-op when the builder is the auditor or has registered before.

steps.title: Privately mint to the builder
steps.notes: The owner generates the mint proof in the browser with the mint circuit at /eerc/circuits/mint (lib/eerc/operations/mint.ts). Studio's runner does it when the deployment signs as the owner, with no popup from a Console wallet.

checks.description: The token is in standalone mode

review: The token reuses the shared Fuji registrar, verifiers and BabyJubJub library from the registry.
Only the owner can mint, and each mint is a proof encrypted to the recipient's and the auditor's keys.
Ownership is two-step: the builder calls acceptOwnership, so the deployer never keeps control.
Every proof and every key stays in the owner's or user's browser.

frontend.summary: A private token: holders see and send balances only they can read, and the issuer mints privately to members.
audience: Holders who receive and send the token privately
The issuer, who mints to registered members
journeys: Set up once: 'Create your private account' with one wallet signature, explained as the key that unlocks your balance.
See your balance, decrypted in the browser, with a note on who else can see it (nobody, or the auditor if the token has one).
Send privately to a member, with a check that they have a private account and a progress line while the privacy proof is generated.
Issuer area, shown only to the owner: pick a member, enter an amount, mint privately.
flows: Load the eerc skill and start from its templates; every screen uses useEERC('EncryptedERC') from @studio/react.
Everything happens in the app: never link holders or the issuer to Builder Hub's eERC console to register, send, mint or see a balance.
Issuer: mint(recipient, amount) from the owner-only Mint screen, after isRegistered(recipient).
Holder: register() once, then show balance.formatted (unlock() on a new device); transfer(to, amount) after isRegistered(to).
